_about: Curated figures for /landmark-numbers/uk-and-nations/. Each measure gives a value for the UK and each nation, with its period and source. Formats: int, km2, years1, pct1, pct2, money, money2, m1 (millions), dec2. A null value shows as a dash. The quarterly Claude scheduled task checks these and opens a pull request when newer figures are published.

groups.note: Output is gross value added: the value of goods and services produced, minus what went into making them. GDP adds taxes on products. The UK figures include offshore oil and gas, which isn't counted in any nation, so the nations add up to slightly less than the UK. Regional figures are revised less often than national ones, so the UK total here (for 2024) is a little below the latest national estimate for the same year.

measures.source: NAEI for DESNZ and the devolved governments, Greenhouse gas inventories for England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland: 1990–2024 (May 2026), table 19; excludes international aviation and shipping

measures.label: Greenhouse gas emissions per person (tonnes CO₂e)
measures.source: NAEI for DESNZ and the devolved governments, Greenhouse gas inventories for England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland: 1990–2024 (May 2026), table 19; excludes international aviation and shipping; divided by ONS mid-2024 population

groups.note: Shares are of electricity generated in each nation. The grid is shared, so a nation can generate more than it uses and send the rest to the others or abroad (Northern Ireland shares a market with Ireland). The UK row of "sent out or brought in" is net imports through interconnectors. Emissions are for 2024, the latest year with figures for each nation. The UK total includes 10.0 million tonnes from offshore oil and gas that isn't assigned to any nation.

measures.label: Reoffending within a year after release from prison (%)

justice.note: The three systems count differently and publish at different times, so each figure shows its own date. Scotland counts homicide victims; England and Wales and Northern Ireland count offences. With small numbers, homicide rates can swing from year to year. Recorded crime isn't shown because each system uses different counting rules. Reoffending is measured differently in each system (Scotland counts reconvictions), so compare the three with care.
